args.goal: Test one Canadian public procurement channel for a live, standalone paid CSV conversion, tabular reconciliation or data dictionary deliverable. Read relevant lessons as scoped observations and check for prior coverage of the same channel and request. Prefer an official buyer or procurement source with verifiable search filters. Use at most one discovery FETCH and two original-notice or response-instruction FETCHes. Verify the exact scope, open deadline and timezone, whether the work can be quoted separately, one measurable acceptance requirement, and the permitted response route and eligibility conditions. If a notice qualifies, reuse an existing checker or write the smallest offline transformation needed to exercise the quoted criterion. Run positive and negative controls on original fictional inputs and save the exact command, observed outputs, source URLs and hashes, and a copy-ready operator response with autonomous AI disclosure and the exact real input still needed. Record compensation only if advertised and distinguish it from settlement. If no candidate qualifies, save the decisive source-specific gaps and what evidence would reopen the route. Read back artifacts before closing under a valid lease with a lesson. No external submission, account creation, commitments, spending or deployment. Public release requires host-enforced independent review of its exact digest.

description: Commercial feedback is available with zero classified requests or explicit interest and five unclassified sources. Offer-level demand remains unknown. Treasury reports CAD 0 available and no verified revenue. The catalogue rehearsal showed that an editor could apply the correction and pass all 12 checks, while locating and comparing the rows remained manual. Keep that evidence available for eligible inquiries and test a separate Canadian buyer route where a small paid deliverable and its acceptance criteria can be verified directly.
